basic.title: Introduction to Data Science
basic.description: Overview of data science lifecycle, business problem formulation, and data-driven decision making.
learningObjectives: Understand the data science lifecycle
Distinguish data science from software engineering
Identify core stages from collection to insight

basic.title: What Is Data?
basic.description: The nature of data, observations, records, attributes, and how digital information represents the physical world.
learningObjectives: Define data, variables, and observations
Understand digital representations of phenomena
Recognize data value types

basic.title: Types of Data
basic.description: Qualitative vs quantitative, discrete vs continuous, nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio measurement scales.
learningObjectives: Classify variables into categorical vs numerical
Differentiate discrete and continuous metrics
Understand Stevens' 4 measurement scales

basic.title: Structured and Unstructured Data
basic.description: Relational tables and columnar schemas vs natural language, imagery, audio, and semi-structured JSON/XML formats.
learningObjectives: Distinguish relational tabular data from text and images
Understand JSON semi-structured payloads
Evaluate data ingestion strategies

basic.title: Database Tables
basic.description: Schema design, primary and foreign keys, normalized relational tables, and row-column indexing.
learningObjectives: Understand relational schemas and constraints
Differentiate primary and foreign keys
Recognize tabular row-column cardinality

basic.title: Python for Data Science
basic.description: Python execution environments, package managers, virtual environments, and data analysis primitives.
learningObjectives: Set up Python analytical environments
Master variables, loops, and list comprehensions
Understand package importing and namespace management

basic.title: Python Functions
basic.description: Modularity, pure functions, lambda expressions, map-filter transformations, and error handling in data workflows.
learningObjectives: Author parameterized reusable functions
Apply lambda and map-filter transforms
Implement defensive validation on input records

basic.title: NumPy Fundamentals
basic.description: N-dimensional array representation, vectorized arithmetic, broadcasting semantics, and contiguous memory storage.
learningObjectives: Create and manipulate ndarrays
Harness vectorized element-wise math
Understand broadcasting rules and performance speedups

basic.title: Pandas Fundamentals
basic.description: Series and DataFrame structures, labeled indices, fast tabular slicing, and data ingestion from CSV/SQL.
learningObjectives: Differentiate Pandas Series and DataFrames
Load tabular data from disk into memory
Inspect schema types and dimensions

basic.title: DataFrames
basic.description: Advanced index selection with loc and iloc, boolean masking, column assignments, and multi-index grouping.
learningObjectives: Execute label-based and position-based indexing
Filter rows using compound boolean logic
Transform and derive new feature columns

basic.title: Data Types
basic.description: Memory footprint of data types: int8/32/64, float32/64, category dtypes, timestamps, and parsing issues.
learningObjectives: Audit memory usage of column types
Cast categorical text to category dtypes
Handle timestamp and date parsing correctly

basic.title: Data Collection
basic.description: Sourcing data via REST APIs, web scraping ethical protocols, streaming telemetry, and batch file extraction.
learningObjectives: Identify trustworthy data sources and extraction techniques
Understand API query parameters and JSON response parsing
Handle extraction pagination and error retry

basic.title: Data Preparation
basic.description: Auditing raw tables, identifying schema inconsistencies, validating boundary conditions, and structuring pipelines.
learningObjectives: Assess data quality across completeness and validity
Establish standard preparation workflows
Profile summary statistics of incoming feeds

basic.title: Missing Values
basic.description: Diagnosing MCAR, MAR, and MNAR missing data mechanisms; dropping rows vs median, mode, and KNN imputation.
learningObjectives: Distinguish missingness mechanisms (MCAR/MAR/MNAR)
Choose appropriate imputation strategies
Avoid leakage during train/test imputation

basic.title: Duplicate Data
basic.description: Detecting exact and fuzzy duplicate rows, primary key collisions, and deduplication retention logic.
learningObjectives: Identify exact duplicate observations
Understand fuzzy string matching for near-duplicates
Select appropriate deduplication retention rules

basic.title: Data Cleaning
basic.description: Comprehensive data hygiene: trimming whitespace, type coercion, string normalization, and sentinel replacements.
learningObjectives: Standardize text representations across columns
Coerce anomalous values into valid numeric ranges
Build clean automated cleaning scripts

basic.title: Introduction to Statistics
basic.description: Descriptive vs inferential statistics, population parameters vs sample statistics, and observational studies.
learningObjectives: Differentiate population parameters from sample metrics
Understand random sampling bias
Interpret summary statistics critically

basic.title: Mean, Median, and Mode
basic.description: Measures of central tendency: arithmetic/geometric mean, median robustness to extreme values, and modal peaks.
learningObjectives: Calculate mean, median, and mode
Evaluate skewness impact on mean vs median
Select the optimal central metric for skewed distributions

basic.title: Percentiles
basic.description: Quantiles, quartiles, interquartile range (IQR), and visual interpretation of five-number summary boxplots.
learningObjectives: Compute percentiles and quartile boundaries
Calculate Interquartile Range (IQR)
Construct and read box-and-whisker plots

basic.title: Variance
basic.description: Quantifying spread: squared deviations from the mean, degrees of freedom, and population vs sample variance (Bessel's correction).
learningObjectives: Calculate squared sum of deviations
Understand Bessel's n-1 correction for sample variance
Interpret dispersion as statistical uncertainty

basic.title: Standard Deviation
basic.description: Square root of variance in native data units, empirical 68-95-99.7 rule, and z-score standard normalization.
learningObjectives: Compute standard deviation from variance
Apply the 68-95-99.7 empirical rule
Standardize raw values into z-scores

intermediate.title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
intermediate.description: Univariate and bivariate profiling, missingness maps, anomaly detection, and systematic hypothesis generation.
learningObjectives: Formulate targeted analytical questions
Conduct univariate and bivariate diagnostic sweeps
Identify data artifacts before modeling

intermediate.title: Data Visualization
intermediate.description: Grammar of graphics, perceptual color theory, chart typography, and choosing effective visual encodings.
learningObjectives: Map data aesthetics to position, color, and size
Select optimal visual forms for distributions vs relationships
Avoid misleading chart truncations and junk

intermediate.title: Histograms and Scatter Plots
intermediate.description: Frequency binning, density estimation, multi-dimensional scatter matrices, and detecting non-linear clustering.
learningObjectives: Optimize histogram bin widths to reveal multimodal peaks
Interpret 2D scatter co-movements and heteroscedasticity
Identify clusters and bivariate anomalies visually

intermediate.title: Correlation
intermediate.description: Measuring linear association: Pearson correlation coefficient r, bounds [-1.0, +1.0], and covariance scaling.
learningObjectives: Derive covariance and Pearson correlation r
Interpret positive, negative, and zero correlation
Recognize strong vs weak linear associations

intermediate.title: Correlation Matrix
intermediate.description: Pairwise correlation heatmaps, symmetric matrices, identifying feature collinearity, and masking redundant pairs.
learningObjectives: Generate multi-feature correlation matrices
Interpret heatmap gradients and color divergent scales
Detect highly correlated feature pairs for pruning

intermediate.title: Correlation vs Causation
intermediate.description: Confounding variables, spurious correlations, Simpson's paradox, and causal diagram fundamentals.
learningObjectives: Differentiate statistical correlation from causal impact
Explain how confounders create false associations
Analyze real-world examples of Simpson's paradox

intermediate.title: Probability
intermediate.description: Sample spaces, events, marginal probability, joint probability, and the fundamental axioms of probability.
learningObjectives: Compute marginal, joint, and union probabilities
Apply the addition and multiplication rules
Understand complementary and mutually exclusive events

intermediate.title: Probability Distributions
intermediate.description: Discrete vs continuous probability distributions: PMF, PDF, CDF, expected value, and moments.
learningObjectives: Differentiate probability mass (PMF) and density (PDF)
Integrate cumulative distribution functions (CDF)
Calculate expected value E[X] and theoretical variance

intermediate.title: Normal Distribution
intermediate.description: The Gaussian bell curve, Central Limit Theorem, standard normal Z-distribution, and tail probability calculation.
learningObjectives: Understand the parameters μ and σ² of the Gaussian PDF
Apply Central Limit Theorem to sample means
Compute tail probabilities and confidence areas

intermediate.title: Sampling
intermediate.description: Simple random sampling, stratified sampling, cluster sampling, and sampling distribution of the mean.
learningObjectives: Evaluate random vs stratified sampling techniques
Minimize selection and survivorship bias
Understand standard error of the mean SE = σ/√n

intermediate.title: Hypothesis Testing
intermediate.description: Null hypothesis (H₀) vs alternative (H₁), test statistics, rejection regions, and Type I (α) vs Type II (β) errors.
learningObjectives: Formulate null and alternative research hypotheses
Calculate test statistics (Z and t)
Determine decision boundaries and statistical power

intermediate.title: Confidence Intervals
intermediate.description: Point estimates vs interval estimates, critical values, margin of error, and interpreting 95% confidence bands.
learningObjectives: Construct confidence intervals for sample means
Interpret the precise frequentist definition of confidence
Assess sample size impact on interval precision

intermediate.title: Linear Functions
intermediate.description: Algebra of straight lines: y = mx + c, rate of change, slope polarity, and linear coordinate systems.
learningObjectives: Interpret slope as rate of change Δy/Δx
Understand intercept as baseline value when x=0
Evaluate linear mappings in feature space

intermediate.title: Plotting Functions
intermediate.description: Evaluating mathematical functions across discrete intervals, domain boundaries, and plotting curves with Matplotlib.
learningObjectives: Discretize continuous function domains
Render symbolic mathematical equations graphically
Inspect inflection points and intersections

intermediate.title: Slope and Intercept
intermediate.description: Geometric and analytical properties of slope m and intercept c; rotation and translation of hyperplanes.
learningObjectives: Calculate slope algebraically between two coordinates
Translate lines using the intercept term
Connect linear parameters to regression weights

intermediate.title: Linear Regression
intermediate.description: Fitting a line of best fit to observations by minimizing sum of squared errors via Ordinary Least Squares.
learningObjectives: Formulate simple linear regression y = β₀ + β₁x + ε
Minimize the residual sum of squares (RSS)
Interpret model coefficients in domain context

intermediate.title: Regression Tables
intermediate.description: Interpreting statsmodels output tables: coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, and F-statistic.
learningObjectives: Read comprehensive OLS summary output tables
Evaluate model fit via F-test of overall significance
Check individual coefficient standard errors

intermediate.title: Regression Coefficients
intermediate.description: Interpretation of intercept β₀ and slope β₁, unit scaling, elasticity, and standardized beta coefficients.
learningObjectives: Interpret marginal unit change in y per unit x
Standardize variables to compare relative feature impact
Recognize omitted variable bias on coefficients

intermediate.title: Residuals
intermediate.description: Observed minus predicted error eᵢ = yᵢ - ŷᵢ, residual plots, homoscedasticity, and checking Gauss-Markov assumptions.
learningObjectives: Compute individual and aggregate residuals
Plot residuals vs fitted values to detect non-linearity
Verify zero-mean and constant variance of errors

intermediate.title: R-Squared
intermediate.description: Coefficient of determination R² = 1 - (SS_res / SS_tot), variance explained, and adjusted R² for multiple predictors.
learningObjectives: Calculate R-squared and explain its variance ratio
Distinguish R² from Pearson correlation r²
Use Adjusted R² to penalize redundant predictors

intermediate.title: Regression P-Values
intermediate.description: Testing null hypothesis that coefficient β₁ = 0, significance thresholds (α=0.05), and confidence intervals on slopes.
learningObjectives: Conduct t-tests on individual regression slopes
Interpret p-values against significance thresholds
Construct 95% confidence intervals on slopes

intermediate.title: Multiple Linear Regression
intermediate.description: Modeling with multiple predictors: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + ... + ε, matrix formulation (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy, and partial effects.
learningObjectives: Formulate multiple linear regression in matrix notation
Interpret partial regression coefficients controlling for covariates
Detect multicollinearity among independent variables

intermediate.title: Data Transformation
intermediate.description: Log transformations, square root, Box-Cox, handling right-skewed revenue/income, and normalizing heteroscedasticity.
learningObjectives: Apply log and Box-Cox power transforms to stabilize variance
Normalize heavily right-skewed target variables
Inverse-transform model predictions back to original scale

intermediate.title: Feature Engineering
intermediate.description: Creating interaction terms, polynomial terms, binning continuous variables, date-time cyclical decomposition, and one-hot encoding.
learningObjectives: Construct non-linear polynomial features and interactions
Decompose timestamp features into cyclical components
Encode categorical variables via one-hot and target encoding

advanced.title: Advanced Statistical Analysis
advanced.description: ANOVA (One-Way and Two-Way), post-hoc Tukey tests, non-parametric tests (Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis), and bootstrap resampling.
learningObjectives: Conduct ANOVA across multiple sample cohorts
Apply non-parametric rank tests when normality is violated
Generate bootstrap empirical confidence intervals

advanced.title: Inferential Statistics
advanced.description: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), Bayesian updating, prior and posterior distributions, and credible intervals.
learningObjectives: Derive Maximum Likelihood Estimators analytically
Understand Bayes' theorem in parameter estimation
Compare Bayesian credible intervals with frequentist confidence intervals

advanced.title: Statistical Significance
advanced.description: Multiple testing corrections (Bonferroni, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR), statistical power analysis, and Cohen's d effect size.
learningObjectives: Control False Discovery Rate (FDR) across hundreds of tests
Calculate Cohen's d to quantify real effect magnitude
Conduct power analysis to determine required sample size

advanced.title: Advanced Regression Analysis
advanced.description: Generalized Linear Models (GLMs), Poisson regression for count data, Logistic link functions, and Weighted Least Squares (WLS).
learningObjectives: Formulate exponential family GLMs with link functions
Fit Poisson regression models to arrival count data
Apply Weighted Least Squares to address heteroscedasticity

advanced.title: Model Assumptions
advanced.description: Rigorous verification of Gauss-Markov conditions: Linearity, Independence (Durbin-Watson), Homoscedasticity (Breusch-Pagan), and Normality (Q-Q plots).
learningObjectives: Execute statistical diagnostic tests for regression assumptions
Interpret Normal Q-Q probability plots
Implement remedies when independence or homoscedasticity fail

advanced.title: Multicollinearity
advanced.description: Detecting inflated standard errors: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF), condition indices, and resolving redundancy via regularization or PCA.
learningObjectives: Calculate Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) for all predictors
Identify condition index matrix instability
Resolve collinearity via feature selection, ridge penalty, or PCA

advanced.title: Outlier Analysis
advanced.description: Leverage points, Cook's distance, studentized residuals, Mahalanobis multivariate distance, and robust M-estimation.
learningObjectives: Distinguish high-leverage outliers from influential points
Compute Cook's distance to flag destabilizing observations
Implement robust Huber loss and RANSAC regressions

advanced.title: Advanced Data Visualization
advanced.description: Interactive dashboards with Plotly/D3, multi-dimensional parallel coordinate plots, geographic chloropleths, and hierarchical sunburst charts.
learningObjectives: Design interactive multi-tiered visual exploration tools
Build parallel coordinate charts for hyperparameter landscapes
Construct spatial geographic representations and heatmaps

advanced.title: Time Series Analysis
advanced.description: Stationarity (ADF test), trend and seasonal decomposition, autocorrelation (ACF/PACF), ARIMA, and exponential smoothing.
learningObjectives: Test for stationarity using the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test
Decompose series into trend, seasonal, and residual components
Interpret ACF and PACF plots to identify AR and MA order

advanced.title: Data Storytelling
advanced.description: Translating quantitative models into strategic executive narratives, cognitive load reduction, and stakeholder decision decks.
learningObjectives: Structure analytical narratives around business impact
Eliminate visual clutter to minimize cognitive load
Tailor technical findings for executive decision makers

advanced.title: Advanced Feature Engineering
advanced.description: Target encoding with out-of-fold regularization, automated feature synthesis, text embeddings, and dimensionality reduction projections.
learningObjectives: Implement leak-free out-of-fold target encoding
Extract dense representations using learned embeddings
Evaluate mutual information scores for feature ranking

advanced.title: Real-World Data Analysis
advanced.description: Wrangling noisy, multi-table production datasets with real-world artifacts: survivorship bias, asynchronous time delays, and drift.
learningObjectives: Tackle messy real-world schemas with missing documentation
Reconcile asynchronous streaming logs and batch records
Detect covariate shift and data distribution drift

advanced.title: End-to-End Data Science Projects
advanced.description: Architecting a production data product: problem framing, data pipelines, statistical validation, model serving, and business KPIs.
learningObjectives: Execute a full-lifecycle analytical initiative from scratch
Deploy reproducible pipelines and statistical checks
Deliver measurable business value and ROI metrics

advanced.title: Case Studies
advanced.description: In-depth dissections of landmark data science initiatives in churn reduction, dynamic pricing, and healthcare epidemiology.
learningObjectives: Deconstruct real-world enterprise architectures
Analyze tradeoffs between model interpretability and predictive lift
Evaluate failure modes and post-mortem learnings

basic.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
basic.description: History of AI, Turing tests, symbolic reasoning vs connectionist paradigms, and modern statistical learning.
learningObjectives: Understand the evolution of AI from rules to learning
Identify key components of intelligent systems
Differentiate narrow AI from general AI concepts

basic.title: AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning
basic.description: Taxonomy of intelligent systems: concentric hierarchy of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Neural Networks.
learningObjectives: Map the subset relationships between AI, ML, and DL
Explain when hand-crafted rules fail and learning succeeds
Identify appropriate problem domains for each paradigm

resources.title: AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning Overview

basic.title: What Is Machine Learning?
basic.description: Tom Mitchell's formal definition: improving performance measure P at task T through experience E.
learningObjectives: State Mitchell's definition of machine learning (T, P, E)
Understand inductive bias and generalization
Identify the core lifecycle of training and inference

basic.title: Types of Machine Learning
basic.description: Overview of the primary learning paradigms: Supervised, Unsupervised, Semi-Supervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
learningObjectives: Differentiate the primary learning modalities
Identify presence or absence of ground truth supervision
Map commercial use cases to the correct learning type

basic.title: Supervised Learning
basic.description: Learning a mapping function f(x) -> y from labeled input-output pairs; regression vs classification tasks.
learningObjectives: Understand the labeled pair paradigm {(x_i, y_i)}
Distinguish continuous targets from discrete classes
Formulate error minimization objectives

basic.title: Unsupervised Learning
basic.description: Discovering latent structure, density estimation, clustering, and manifold projection in unlabeled data.
learningObjectives: Explain learning without explicit ground truth labels
Identify clustering and dimensionality reduction goals
Evaluate latent structure discovery

basic.title: Reinforcement Learning
basic.description: Agent-environment interactions, state-action-reward loops, Markov Decision Processes, and credit assignment.
learningObjectives: Understand the agent, environment, state, action, and reward loop
Differentiate exploration vs exploitation tradeoffs
Recognize delayed reward and credit assignment

basic.title: ML Terminology
basic.description: Essential glossary: parameters vs hyperparameters, epochs, batches, loss vs metric, baseline, and inference.
learningObjectives: Define parameters vs hyperparameters clearly
Understand epochs, batch size, and iteration count
Distinguish training loss from evaluation metrics

basic.title: Python for Machine Learning
basic.description: Setting up data pipelines, reproducible seed configurations, matrix operations, and ML project structures.
learningObjectives: Configure reproducible random seed environments
Perform matrix transformations for feature tables
Organize clean modular ML codebases

basic.title: NumPy and Pandas for ML
basic.description: Extracting feature matrices X and label vectors y from DataFrames, array reshapes, and memory alignment.
learningObjectives: Separate feature matrix X from target vector y
Ensure 2D array shapes for scikit-learn estimators
Perform fast vectorized data transformations

resources.title: NumPy and Pandas for ML Overview

basic.title: Introduction to Scikit-learn
basic.description: The universal estimator API: fit(), transform(), predict(), score(), and pipeline composing principles.
learningObjectives: Master the estimator interface: fit() and predict()
Understand transformer interface: fit_transform()
Evaluate model accuracy using built-in score()

basic.title: Understanding Datasets
basic.description: Dataset morphology: tabular benchmarks (Iris, Boston, Churn), sparsity, class balance, and data generation.
learningObjectives: Inspect feature dimensions and sample size cardinality
Identify sparsity in tabular matrices
Assess class imbalance ratios before training

basic.title: Features and Labels
basic.description: Independent explanatory features vs dependent target labels, target leakage identification, and metadata.
learningObjectives: Define independent predictors vs dependent target variable
Identify target leakage indicators
Structure tidy feature tables

basic.title: Training and Testing Data
basic.description: Out-of-sample generalization, train-test splits, stratified splits, and the golden rule of machine learning.
learningObjectives: Explain why training and testing data must be strictly isolated
Perform stratified train-test splits preserving class ratios
Avoid evaluating models on memorized samples

basic.title: Data Preprocessing
basic.description: Pipeline preprocessing: imputation, handling categorical text, log scaling, and preventing data leakage.
learningObjectives: Fit preprocessors strictly on training data
Transform test data using training parameters
Construct leak-free preparation pipelines

basic.title: Feature Scaling
basic.description: Standardization (Z-score) vs Min-Max Normalization, why distance-based and gradient-based algorithms require scaling.
learningObjectives: Apply StandardScaler (μ=0, σ=1) and MinMaxScaler [0, 1]
Explain why distance algorithms (KNN, SVM, PCA) require scaling
Observe gradient descent convergence speedups with scaled inputs

basic.title: Linear Functions and Graphs
basic.description: Hyperplanes in 2D and ND, decision boundaries, dot products as projections, and geometric intuition of linear models.
learningObjectives: Plot straight line equations y = w·x + b
Visualize hyperplanes partitioning feature space
Understand the normal vector to a decision surface

basic.title: Scatter Plots
basic.description: Visualizing 2D feature distributions, class separation, linear separability, and cluster boundaries.
learningObjectives: Plot 2D feature scatter plots color-coded by class
Assess whether data clusters are linearly separable
Identify non-linear distribution shapes visually

basic.title: Perceptrons
basic.description: Rosenblatt's Perceptron: linear combination wᵀx + b, step activation threshold, and iterative mistake-driven updates.
learningObjectives: Calculate weighted sum z = Σ wᵢxᵢ + b
Apply step activation threshold to classify samples
Understand the Perceptron Learning Algorithm update rule

basic.title: Introduction to Regression
basic.description: Continuous target estimation, Mean Squared Error loss, line of best fit, and regression vs classification comparison.
learningObjectives: Define regression as predicting continuous scalar values
Formulate the Mean Squared Error (MSE) objective function
Evaluate simple linear predictors on synthetic data

basic.title: Introduction to Classification
basic.description: Discrete category prediction, decision boundaries, class probabilities, and binary vs multiclass tasks.
learningObjectives: Define classification as predicting discrete class categories
Understand decision boundary partition of feature space
Differentiate binary classification from multiclass and multilabel

intermediate.title: Linear Regression
intermediate.description: Ordinary Least Squares, closed-form normal equations (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy, gradient descent optimization, and evaluation.
learningObjectives: Derive the closed-form OLS normal equations
Fit linear regression models with Scikit-learn
Compute residuals and evaluate R² score

intermediate.title: Multiple Linear Regression
intermediate.description: Modeling with N features, matrix formulation, partial slopes, multicollinearity detection, and feature selection.
learningObjectives: Fit multiple linear regression models across multidimensional feature matrices
Interpret partial regression coefficients
Evaluate feature importance and multicollinearity risks

intermediate.title: Polynomial Regression
intermediate.description: Modeling non-linear relationships via polynomial feature basis expansions x, x², x³ and controlling model degree.
learningObjectives: Transform linear features into polynomial space
Fit non-linear curves using linear regression machinery
Observe how high degree polynomials lead directly to overfitting

intermediate.title: Logistic Regression
intermediate.description: Binary classification via sigmoid squashing σ(z), log-odds (logit), maximum likelihood estimation, and decision thresholds.
learningObjectives: Derive log-odds and the Sigmoid squashing function
Interpret model output as calibrated class probabilities P(y=1|x)
Tune classification threshold to adjust precision and recall

intermediate.title: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
intermediate.description: Non-parametric instance-based learning, Euclidean/Manhattan distance metrics, voting rule, and the curse of dimensionality.
learningObjectives: Implement distance-based k-nearest voting for classification and regression
Analyze the impact of hyperparameter k on decision boundary smoothness
Recognize distance breakdown in high-dimensional spaces

intermediate.title: Decision Trees
intermediate.description: Hierarchical binary splitting, Shannon Entropy, Information Gain, Gini Impurity, and tree pruning strategies.
learningObjectives: Calculate Gini Impurity and Information Gain for splits
Construct recursive binary decision tree rules
Tune max_depth and min_samples_split to prevent overfitting

intermediate.title: Random Forest
intermediate.description: Ensemble bagging of decision trees, bootstrap sample aggregation, random feature subset selection, and out-of-bag error.
learningObjectives: Explain how averaging decorrelated trees reduces variance
Implement Random Forest classifiers and regressors
Inspect Out-Of-Bag (OOB) error estimates as validation

intermediate.title: Naive Bayes
intermediate.description: Bayes' theorem applied to classification, conditional independence assumption, Gaussian, Multinomial, and Bernoulli variants.
learningObjectives: Formulate Bayes' rule P(y|x) ∝ P(y) ∏ P(xᵢ|y)
Understand the conditional independence assumption
Apply Multinomial Naive Bayes to text classification

intermediate.title: Support Vector Machines
intermediate.description: Maximum margin hyperplanes, support vectors, soft-margin slack variables (C parameter), and non-linear kernel trick (RBF).
learningObjectives: Understand maximum margin separation geometry
Tune soft-margin penalty C balancing margin width and violations
Project non-linearly separable points using RBF kernels

intermediate.title: K-Means Clustering
intermediate.description: Centroid-based unsupervised partitioning, Voronoi cells, Expectation-Maximization iteration, k-means++ seeding, and elbow heuristic.
learningObjectives: Step through Lloyd's algorithm: assign points, recompute centroids
Compute Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (Inertia)
Apply the elbow method and Silhouette scores to determine optimal k

intermediate.title: Hierarchical Clustering
intermediate.description: Agglomerative bottom-up merging vs divisive top-down clustering, linkage criteria (single, complete, Ward), and dendrogram cutting.
learningObjectives: Construct hierarchical cluster trees and read dendrograms
Compare single, complete, and Ward linkage criteria
Determine cluster cuts based on distance thresholds

intermediate.title: DBSCAN
intermediate.description: Density-based spatial clustering: epsilon neighborhoods, min_samples threshold, core points, border points, and noise handling.
learningObjectives: Differentiate core points, border points, and noise outliers
Cluster arbitrary non-convex geometries (rings, spirals)
Tune epsilon ε and min_samples hyperparameters

intermediate.title: Dimensionality Reduction
intermediate.description: Curse of dimensionality: exponential volume expansion, distance concentration, computational cost, and compression goals.
learningObjectives: Understand the geometric curse of dimensionality
Explain how high dimensions degrade distance metrics
Formulate dimensionality reduction as information preservation

intermediate.title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
intermediate.description: Orthogonal linear transformation, covariance matrix eigendecomposition, maximum variance axes, and scree plots.
learningObjectives: Compute eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the covariance matrix
Project high-dimensional data onto top principal components
Interpret explained variance ratio and scree plots

intermediate.title: Model Training
intermediate.description: The mechanics of iterative parameter fitting: loss evaluation, weight updates, convergence criteria, and training logs.
learningObjectives: Inspect training convergence logs and loss trajectories
Implement early stopping based on validation plateaus
Ensure deterministic reproducibility during training

intermediate.title: Model Testing
intermediate.description: Evaluating unseen test sets, computing test generalization gap, statistical significance of model differences, and test hygiene.
learningObjectives: Evaluate final candidate models on pristine held-out test data
Calculate generalization error gap between train and test
Maintain test set integrity by preventing feedback loops

intermediate.title: Validation Data
intermediate.description: Three-way data splits: Train, Validation, and Test sets; hyperparameter tuning without test set contamination.
learningObjectives: Partition datasets into 60/20/20 train/validation/test splits
Use validation sets strictly for hyperparameter selection
Prevent subtle information leakage into final test benchmarks

intermediate.title: Cross-Validation
intermediate.description: K-Fold, Stratified K-Fold, TimeSeriesSplit, and leave-one-out cross validation for low-variance performance estimation.
learningObjectives: Implement K-Fold cross validation and compute mean ± std scores
Use Stratified K-Fold for imbalanced classification
Apply TimeSeriesSplit without looking into future records

intermediate.title: Confusion Matrix
intermediate.description: True Positives (TP), False Positives (FP), True Negatives (TN), False Negatives (FN), Type I vs Type II classification errors.
learningObjectives: Construct and read 2x2 binary confusion matrices
Identify costs of Type I (false alarm) vs Type II (missed event) errors
Extend confusion matrices to multi-class evaluation heatmaps

intermediate.title: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score
intermediate.description: Why accuracy fails on imbalanced data, Precision = TP/(TP+FP), Recall = TP/(TP+FN), Harmonic Mean F1, and PR-AUC.
learningObjectives: Explain why accuracy is misleading when classes are 99:1
Derive Precision, Recall, and F1 Score mathematically
Optimize decision thresholds for precision-centric vs recall-centric use cases

resources.title: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score Overview

intermediate.title: Regression Evaluation Metrics
intermediate.description: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and R².
learningObjectives: Compare MAE robustness to outliers vs MSE quadratic penalty
Interpret RMSE in native target units
Calculate MAPE and evaluate percentage relative error

intermediate.title: Overfitting and Underfitting
intermediate.description: High variance vs high bias regimes, learning curves, training vs validation error divergence, and diagnostics.
learningObjectives: Diagnose overfitting when training loss drops but validation loss climbs
Identify underfitting when model capacity is insufficient
Plot learning curves over varying sample sizes

intermediate.title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
intermediate.description: Decomposition of expected prediction error: Error = Bias² + Variance + Irreducible Noise; finding optimal model complexity.
learningObjectives: Formulate the mathematical error decomposition E[(y - ŷ)²]
Explain how simple models exhibit high bias and complex models high variance
Select model complexity that minimizes total generalization error

advanced.title: Regularization: L1 and L2
advanced.description: Shrinkage methods: L1 Lasso (|w|) driving sparse feature selection vs L2 Ridge (w²) shrinking collinear weights, and ElasticNet.
learningObjectives: Add L1 and L2 penalties to cost functions J(w) + λ||w||
Explain geometric sparsity created by L1 diamond contours
Tune regularization strength λ via cross validation

advanced.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
advanced.description: Systematic search strategies, validation score surfaces, exploration budgets, and preventing overfitting on validation folds.
learningObjectives: Structure hyperparameter search spaces logically
